entries.title: DCOM permission warning (harmless)
entries.what: A Windows component tried to start a COM server without the matching permission. Microsoft documents these as expected and safe to ignore; changing the permissions can break things.
fix: Safe to ignore - do not change DCOM permissions

entries.title: COM server did not register in time
entries.what: A COM server did not register with DCOM within the timeout. Usually a background app that was slow to start; harmless if nothing is broken.
causes: Slow startup of a background app
fix: Safe to ignore unless a specific feature fails

entries.title: DCOM could not start a disabled service
entries.what: DCOM tried to start a service that is disabled. Harmless if you disabled that service on purpose.

entries.title: DCOM could not reach a computer
entries.what: DCOM could not communicate with another computer (often a monitoring or management tool polling an offline PC).
fix: Harmless if the named computer is gone; otherwise check its connectivity

entries.title: WMI event filter could not be reactivated
entries.what: A WMI event filter query failed at startup (classic leftover of an old component). Harmless.

entries.title: Performance counter could not be opened
entries.what: A performance counter DLL failed to open. Affects only monitoring tools; harmless.
fix: If performance counters are needed: lodctr /R (as administrator)

entries.title: Performance counter DLL could not be loaded
entries.what: An extensible performance counter could not be loaded. Affects only monitoring tools; harmless.

entries.title: Performance counter problem (harmless)
entries.what: A performance counter could not be opened or loaded. Affects only monitoring tools.

entries.title: Trace session error (harmless)
entries.what: A diagnostic trace session (e.g. ReadyBoot, Circular Kernel Context Logger) stopped or could not start. Developer diagnostics only.

entries.title: Device registration with Azure AD skipped
entries.what: Windows checked whether to register the device with Azure AD / Entra ID. Harmless on PCs that are not Entra-joined.

entries.title: Database file access error (usually harmless)
entries.what: A Windows internal database (often the usage monitor SRUM or the Windows Search/Store cache) could not open a log file. Common on desktops and usually harmless.
causes: Missing folder for a system database log
fix: Usually ignore; if repeated every minute, recreating the missing folder named in the message stops it

entries.title: Internal database started/stopped
entries.what: A Windows internal database engine instance started, stopped or replayed logs. Routine.

entries.title: Cryptographic Services: VSS writer permission note
entries.what: Cryptographic Services hit an access-denied while preparing a backup snapshot. Known and harmless.

entries.title: Could not extract third-party root list
entries.what: Windows could not process the downloaded trusted root certificate list (often offline or blocked). Usually harmless.

entries.title: VDS: unexpected failure (harmless)
entries.what: The Virtual Disk Service basic provider logged an error, often for card readers or empty removable drives. Harmless.

entries.title: Background transfer (BITS) job
entries.what: A background download job was created, finished or transferred data. Harmless.

entries.title: Time provider is a VM integration service
entries.what: The clock is synchronized from the virtualization host. Normal in virtual machines.

entries.title: File system filter loaded
entries.what: A file system filter driver (antivirus, backup, sync tool) loaded. Normal at boot.

entries.title: Power plan changed
entries.what: The active power plan or power mode changed. Normal.

entries.title: Device metadata/driver retrieval note
entries.what: Device Setup Manager could not get metadata or a driver from the internet for a device. Normal when offline or for generic devices.

entries.title: Microsoft Edge updater status
entries.what: Microsoft Edge update service status record. Harmless.

entries.title: Google updater status
entries.what: Google update service status record. Harmless.

entries.title: Performance counters loaded/unloaded
entries.what: Performance counters were registered or removed (usually during installs/updates). Harmless.

entries.title: Windows license validated
entries.what: Windows license was validated at logon. Harmless.

entries.title: WinRM not listening
entries.what: Windows Remote Management is not configured to accept requests. Normal unless you use remote PowerShell.
